paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the BLEU score performance of four different methods—Consistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE-MP, and Consistency-Bi—as a function of Average Lagging (AL), which ranges from 2.5 to 10.0 on a linear scale along the x-axis. The y-axis represents the BLEU score, ranging from 25 to 33, also on a linear scale, with gridlines at integer intervals. The Consistency-Bi method, shown as a solid red line with star markers, consistently achieves the highest BLEU scores, starting at approximately 29.0 at AL=2.5 and increasing to about 32.0 at AL=10.0. The Inconsistency-CE-MP method, depicted as a dashed blue line with square markers, begins at around 26.2 at AL=2.5 and rises to approximately 31.5 at AL=10.0. The Inconsistency-CE method, shown as a dash-dotted purple line with square markers, starts at roughly 26.0 at AL=2.5 and reaches about 31.2 at AL=10.0. The Consistency-CE method, represented by a dotted purple line with circle markers, starts at approximately 25.8 at AL=2.5 and increases to about 31.0 at AL=10.0. All four lines show a positive trend, with BLEU scores increasing as Average Lagging increases, though the Consistency-Bi method maintains a clear performance advantage throughout the range.
